bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 10200 (libaom): Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free WRITE 2. Crash State: read_uncompressed_header av1_decode_frame_headers_and_setup aom_decode_frame_from_obus. Sanitizer: address (ASAN). Fuzzer: libFuzzer_libaom_av1_dec_fuzzer, target av1_dec_fuzzer.
bug_description.summary: When a new coded video sequence begins (a sequence header that is inconsistent with the previous one, followed by a KEY_FRAME), read_uncompressed_header calls reset_frame_buffers, which unconditionally re-initializes every entry of the frame-buffer pool by writing 'neutral grey' pixels into frame_bufs[i].buf. One of those YV12 buffers still references raw frame storage that was freed/reallocated by a prior frame whose frame size differed, so the neutral-grey store (a 16-bit write in the high-bit-depth path) writes into a freed heap region.

source.description: Project-level parse point where attacker-controlled compressed AV1 frame-header OBU bytes are handed to the frame-header decode logic (av1_decode_frame_headers_and_setup -> read_uncompressed_header). This is the input load that materializes the frame_type and sequence-header state driving the bug.
source.value_from: Untrusted AV1 bitstream bytes (OBU frame header) supplied by the fuzzer testcase and delivered via aom_codec_decode -> aom_decode_frame_from_obus; the bit-reader `rb` over `data` yields the frame_type and the sequence-header parameters that trigger the buffer reset.
source.note: Not scored at LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput / aom_codec_decode: the harness merely feeds bytes. The vulnerability-relevant load is the AV1 OBU frame-header parse.

tainted_value_origin.description: First vulnerability-relevant value materialized from the bitstream: the 2-bit frame_type. A KEY_FRAME on the first frame of a changed sequence is what selects the reset_frame_buffers path; the sequence-header parameters (bit_depth / frame size) parsed earlier decide whether a pool buffer was reallocated.
tainted_value_origin.note: sequence_header_changed is set separately at aom/av1/decoder/obu.c:275 when the newly parsed sequence header is inconsistent with the previous one.

sink.description: ASan crash site: a 16-bit (2-byte) neutral-grey store through base = CONVERT_TO_SHORTPTR(buf->buffers[plane]) writes into raw frame-buffer storage that has already been freed. This is the heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 2.

root_cause.description: reset_frame_buffers unconditionally calls set_planes_to_neutral_grey on every frame_bufs[i].buf in the pool, including buffers that are not the current frame (i != new_fb_idx) and buffers whose raw storage was freed/reallocated by a previous frame that used a different frame size. It performs no check that the buffer is still validly allocated for the current sequence. The fix restricts the reset to the current buffer (cm->new_fb_idx) and only when cur_buf->buffer_alloc_sz >= cur_buf->frame_size, i.e. when the backing allocation is large enough / still valid. The missing guard (buffer_alloc_sz >= frame_size, plus 'only the current buffer') is the defect the patch adds.

parser_admitted.condition: OBU demuxer accepted the input, dispatched an OBU_FRAME_HEADER / OBU_FRAME unit and entered the AV1 frame-header parser (read_frame_header_obu). Confirms the bytes passed container/OBU dispatch and reached the vulnerable frame-setup path; earlier than root cause and sink, later than program entry.

sequence_change_detected.condition: A new sequence header inconsistent with the previous one was observed (pbi->sequence_header_changed == 1).

keyframe_reset_path.condition: The changed-sequence frame is a KEY_FRAME, so reset_frame_buffers is invoked and iterates the whole frame-buffer pool.

coarse_trace.summary: Attacker-controlled AV1 frame-header OBU bytes enter av1_decode_frame_headers_and_setup.
An earlier frame with a different frame size reallocates a pool buffer; aom_realloc_frame_buffer -> av1_get_frame_buffer frees the previously allocated raw frame storage.
A changed sequence header plus a KEY_FRAME selects the reset_frame_buffers path.
Unconditionally calls set_planes_to_neutral_grey on every pool buffer, including one whose raw storage was freed.
16-bit neutral-grey store writes into the freed frame-buffer region (heap-use-after-free WRITE 2).

fine_trace.note: Untrusted AV1 frame-header OBU bytes enter the frame-setup decoder through the bit-reader rb over data.
frame_type is materialized from 2 bitstream bits; KEY_FRAME later gates the reset path.

A newly parsed sequence header is inconsistent with the previous one (are_seq_headers_consistent == 0), e.g. a different bit_depth or frame-size regime; this flag arms the reset path. The differing frame size is also what causes a pool buffer to be reallocated/freed.

Raw frame-buffer storage (the 1612854-byte region) is allocated for a pool slot during an earlier frame's setup_buffer_pool -> aom_realloc_frame_buffer. This is the ASan allocation stack. frame_bufs[slot].buf.buffer_alloc / buffers[plane] point into this region.

A subsequent frame whose frame size no longer fits the slot's allocation reallocates the same internal frame buffer (setup_frame_size decodeframe.c:4704 -> setup_buffer_pool decodeframe.c:2093 -> aom_realloc_frame_buffer yv12config.c:98 -> here), freeing the region allocated in step 4. This is the ASan free stack. The pool entry that still aliases this storage is now dangling.
Guard taken: the changed-sequence branch is entered.
Because the changed-sequence frame is a KEY_FRAME (guard at line 4486: pbi->common.frame_type == KEY_FRAME, taken), reset_frame_buffers is invoked before this frame's own setup_frame_size runs.

In the pool loop, set_planes_to_neutral_grey is called for EVERY frame_bufs[i].buf with no check that the buffer is the current one or still validly allocated. For the slot whose raw storage was freed in step 5, frame_bufs[i].buf.buffers[plane] is dangling. The missing guard (patch adds: only cm->new_fb_idx, and only if cur_buf->buffer_alloc_sz >= cur_buf->frame_size) is the root cause.
High-bit-depth path: base is derived from buf->buffers[plane], which points into the freed region.
16-bit store of val = 1 << (bit_depth - 1) into freed frame-buffer storage: heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 2 (ASan crash at decodeframe.c:99:57).

sanitizer_ground_truth.region: 0x7ffff8ef8a60 is located 516704 bytes inside of 1612854-byte region [0x7ffff8e7a800,0x7ffff9004436)

format.name: AV1 bitstream (OBU / temporal-unit stream decoded by av1_dec_fuzzer)
format.contract: The input must be admitted by the AV1 OBU demuxer and parse as a valid sequence header + frame header stream. To be reachability-comparable it must contain at least two coded frames such that: (1) a first sequence establishes and allocates a frame-buffer-pool entry at one frame size / bit-depth regime, (2) a later sequence header is parsed that is inconsistent with the first (are_seq_headers_consistent == 0, e.g. changed bit_depth or frame-size regime that forces reallocation/free of a pool buffer), and (3) that changed sequence's first frame is a KEY_FRAME so read_uncompressed_header invokes reset_frame_buffers, which then writes neutral-grey pixels into the stale (freed) pool buffer. High-bit-depth (use_highbitdepth) must be in effect to reach the 16-bit store at set_planes_to_neutral_grey. Original PoC bytes are not part of this contract.
